root_cause.text: The function `read_key_from_user_keying()` in `crash_dump_dm_crypt.c` logged the first 8 bytes of the dm-crypt key payload using the `%8ph` format specifier in a debug print statement, which allowed sensitive key material to be exposed in kernel logs when debug logging was enabled.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `%8ph` format specifier and the corresponding key data argument from the `kexec_dprintk` call, as shown by the diff: `-	kexec_dprintk("Get dm crypt key (size=%u) %s: %8ph\n", dm_key->key_size, dm_key->key_desc, dm_key->data);` changed to `+	kexec_dprintk("Get dm crypt key (size=%u) %s\n", dm_key->key_size, dm_key->key_desc);`. The CVE description explicitly states that logging the first 8 bytes of the key payload partially exposes the dm-crypt key.
